title: STM32 sensor hub with a Linux IIO driver
summary: An STM32 Nucleo sensor hub that feeds a Raspberry Pi 4 and is meant to end in a Linux IIO kernel driver. It is a work in progress: the bare-metal foundation is done and the rest is planned.
highlights: Goal: a complete sensor path from bare-metal firmware, through a host link, to a Linux Industrial I/O driver on a Pi 4.
Sensors: an MSA311 accelerometer and an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor.
Done so far: the reset path, vector table, HAL initialization, clock configuration and GPIO setup.
Target deliverable: an IIO kernel driver, written to the standard an upstream review would expect. It is not built yet.

details.label: Why this project
details.body: Most of my firmware work has been on the microcontroller side or on host tooling. I wanted one project that crosses the boundary between bare-metal code and the Linux device model, because that is where the hardest debugging happens: registers, protocols, drivers and kernel interfaces all in one chain.

details.label: Plan
details.body: An STM32 Nucleo reads the sensors and sends the data to a Raspberry Pi 4 over a host link. The Pi exposes the readings through the Linux IIO subsystem, so userspace sees an ordinary IIO device. The MSA311 is the first device, and the ultrasonic sensor follows.

details.label: Where it stands
details.body: The bare-metal foundation is in place (startup and vector table, HAL initialization, clocks, GPIO). The host link and the kernel driver are the next stages. I will add results here when they exist.
